standard.title: Certification Scheme for Occupational Health and Safety Practitioner

notes: WHY module_kind = compliance, and why this is probably the highest-value module in Phase 5. Section 5 states flatly: 'All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai shall employ Certified OHS Practitioners within their organization.' That is a universal, checkable staffing duty resting on a credential with a stated two-year validity, backed by five named pieces of legislation, and it applies to every factory, construction, infrastructure and service business in Dubai — which is precisely the market described in the memory notes for this product. A report can say COMPLIANT or NON-COMPLIANT without interpretation: does the establishment employ a Certified OHS Practitioner whose certificate has not expired, and is that person registered with the Health and Safety Department and up to date. VALIDITY VERSUS INTERVAL, checked specifically per the Phase 3 lesson: this document states a REAL VALIDITY PERIOD — 'a certificate valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance' (section 8.4), restated in the Annex A flowchart note. Renewal must happen BEFORE THE END OF THE SECOND YEAR, so as with GU131 the actionable date precedes the expiry date. Unlike the Lifeguard scheme, no window length is given for how early renewal may start, and unlike the Lifeguard scheme no grace period is mentioned either way — the document simply does not say what happens on the day after expiry. That silence is recorded honestly rather than filled in by analogy with S1. AN UNUSUAL AND COMMERCIALLY IMPORTANT RENEWAL MECHANIC: renewal is by DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE OF CONTINUING COMPETENCE, not by examination, provided the practitioner submits an employment certificate as an OHS practitioner plus evidence of CPD activities covering the past two years. Only those who FAIL to submit that evidence must sit and pass a renewal examination. So the product can materially change a client's outcome: a practitioner whose CPD is captured contemporaneously renews on paperwork, and one whose is not has to sit an exam. That is a concrete, monetisable benefit of tracking CPD in the app, and it is the clearest such case found in this corpus. NOTE ALSO that the CPD requirement is entirely UNQUANTIFIED — no hours, no points, no minimum number of activities — so the app can record CPD but cannot judge sufficiency. THIS DOCUMENT AND ITS SIBLING S2 ARE A MATCHED PAIR issued the same day; S2 covers the OHS Person in Charge. They share the examination conduct rules (one invigilator per 20 candidates, desks 1.25 m apart), the two-year validity and the EIAC/ISO 17024 accreditation frame, and they differ in the entry qualifications and the examination. Read them together; do not assume a clause in one appears in the other. Both also share the invigilation and desk-spacing wording with GU131, which is now the third document in this corpus carrying those same two numbers — evidence that DM reuses a standard examination-conduct block across its certification schemes. EDITION: version V 1.0 and issue date 1 November 2025. The cover prints the date numerically as 1/11/2025, which under rule 2 would be ambiguous (both components <= 12) — but the page-2 document history log prints it in long form as '1st November 2025', which settles day-first from inside the document. catalogue_editions.json records this at HIGH confidence for that reason, and it is followed here. Superseded issue date is printed as 'NEW', so this is a first edition with no predecessor. The source_url sits under /uploads/2025/12/, a month after the stated issue date — the usual upload-versus-issue offset, and another reminder not to read dates off paths. The code DM-HSD-S3 carries no GU number; guideline_no is null. WHAT COULD NOT BE OBTAINED: no list of approved Certification Bodies, no certificate verification route beyond the serial or control number printed on the certificate, no fee schedule (repeatedly deferred to 'as defined by Dubai Municipality'), and no statement of what happens between expiry and renewal. The examination material approval in Annex B is 'valid for a specified period' which the document never specifies — an explicit acknowledgement of a validity with the number omitted.

competencies.requirement: Meet one of four alternative entry routes before sitting the examination: (a) Bachelor's degree in engineering PLUS either a government-approved Diploma in Occupational Health and/or Safety with 2 years' experience, or an international/national Diploma from NEBOSH, BSC, BCSP, Ofqual or NVQ with 2 years' experience; OR (b) Diploma in Engineering PLUS either of those diplomas with 5 years' experience; OR (c) Bachelor of Science PLUS either of those diplomas with 5 years' experience; OR (d) a government-approved Bachelor's degree in occupational health and safety on a 3 to 4 year curriculum with 5 years' work experience. The Certification Body must verify and screen the candidate's qualifications against these before allowing them to proceed. Then pass the certification examination: 100 multiple choice questions with four options and one correct answer, completed within three hours, no reference material permitted, scoring an overall average of at least 60% AND at least 50% in each of Element 2 (Risk Management), Element 3 (Application of Safety Concepts) and Element 6 (Health and Safety Regulations). The role covers designations including Occupational Health and Safety Officers, Advisors, Managers, Engineers and Specialists.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body — a nationally or internationally reputed qualifications provider, UAE licensed, participated in by Dubai Municipality and accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC) to ISO 17024
competencies.renewal_requirement: Renew BEFORE THE END OF THE SECOND YEAR of certification validity. The primary route is documentary: submit to the Certification Body an employment certificate as an occupational health and safety practitioner, plus evidence of activities attended or participated in to improve health and safety knowledge over the past two years (training certificates, training hours, workshops and conferences whether private or government, involvement with professional bodies and campaigns, journal articles). Practitioners who submit that evidence pay only the fees covering evaluation of qualification, registration and certificate. Practitioners who FAIL to submit it must take and pass the certification renewal examination approved by the Health and Safety Department, to the same 60%/50% assessment standard. Certification may also be cancelled and the practitioner reassessed where their establishment obtains an unsatisfactory compliance grade (D or E) at routine DM inspection and further assessment confirms the practitioner's inability, or on the recommendation of the DM OHS Officer conducting inspection monitoring.
competencies.trigger_event: employment as OHS practitioner at any industry in Dubai; and again before the end of the second year of certification validity
competencies.source_quote: To become a Certified OHS Practitioner, the candidate must obtain an overall average mark of at least sixty percent (60%) provided that the candidate achieved a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark for each of these examination elements - Risk Management (Element 2), Application of Safety Concepts (Element 3), and Health and Safety Regulations (Element 6). OHS Practitioner fulfilling all the scheme requirements as outlined in this guideline document and defined by the Accredited Certification Bodies shall receive a certificate valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance. (p10) OHS Practitioner shall renew the certification before the end of the second year of certification validity. (p11)

competencies.requirement: Trained personnel appointed by the Certification Body. Must arrive at the venue ahead of time; at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates. Must supervise candidates throughout the entire examination, remain alert and give their whole attention to its proper conduct, and must not undertake any other activity while invigilating — they cannot act as a reader or writer for a candidate and cannot provide translation or interpretation. Must intervene on inappropriate behaviour including cheating, photographing or copying examination questionnaires, talking or intentionally disturbing other candidates; for serious incidents the examination should be cancelled and the candidate instructed to leave after their answer sheets and examination materials are collected. UNLIKE GU131, this document sets NO education or experience requirement for invigilators at all — GU131 specifies High School or Diploma or NEBOSH/IOSH approval and states experience is not compulsory. The omission is real, not an extraction gap.
competencies.trigger_event: appointment to invigilate a certification examination
competencies.source_quote: Certification Body should appoint trained personnel to act as invigilators. Invigilators must arrive at the venue ahead of time and there should be at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates. (p9-10) Invigilators must not undertake any other activities while invigilating. For example, they cannot act as a reader or writer for any candidate nor provide translations and interpretations.

competencies.requirement: A nationally or internationally reputed qualifications provider, UAE licensed, participated in by Dubai Municipality and accredited by EIAC as per ISO 17024, working in coordination with the Health and Safety Department. Must provide DM-approved examination materials in BOTH Arabic and English; meet ISO 17024 requirements in reviewing the effectiveness of the scheme; provide the H&S Department with access to records and documentation on personnel qualifications and audits, and give officials nominated by the Director access to examination question papers, scripts, marking records and associated documents; maintain a candidate database with access provided to Dubai Municipality; verify and screen candidates' qualifications against the section 6 minimum competency requirements; and have a NAMED POINT OF CONTACT for each certification it delivers, so it is clear to whom candidates, the Department and EIAC direct enquiries. Must always adhere to the quality processes and procedures of the H&S Department and EIAC. The Department intends to develop unified arrangements across all Certification Bodies — a common registration system, coordinated exam planning, a shared examination question database and common records — which all bodies must then follow.
competencies.issuing_body: Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC) accreditation to ISO 17024, in coordination with the DM Health and Safety Department
competencies.renewal_requirement: No accreditation validity period is stated. Accreditation ends if withdrawn by EIAC or if the body ceases operation. Recorded null honestly rather than assuming an ISO cycle.
competencies.trigger_event: before offering OHS Practitioner certification and registration in Dubai
competencies.source_quote: Certification Bodies accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center in coordination with Health and Safety Department can offer OHS Practitioner Certification and Registration in the Emirate of Dubai. The accreditation will be granted as per ISO 17024 Standard by the Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC). Certification Bodies shall provide DM approved examination materials in Arabic and English for OHS Practitioners working in the Emirate of Dubai (see Annex B).

limits.parameter_label: Validity of an OHS Practitioner certificate
limits.display: valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance
limits.qualifier_rule: Runs from the date of issuance — stated unambiguously here, unlike the Lifeguard scheme where three different anchor dates appear. Renewal must be completed before the end of the second year, so the actionable date precedes the expiry date.
limits.source_quote: OHS Practitioner fulfilling all the scheme requirements as outlined in this guideline document and defined by the Accredited Certification Bodies shall receive a certificate valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance. (p10) Note: Issued certificate is valid for a period of two (2) years from the date of issuance. The OHS Practitioner shall undergo renewal of certification before the end of the second year of the certification validity (Refer to Clause 8.6 of the guideline). (Annex A flowchart note, p13)
limits.note: A genuine competency validity, not an examination interval. The document does not state how early renewal may begin, nor what happens between expiry and renewal — there is no grace-period clause either granting or denying one. Both silences are recorded rather than filled from the Lifeguard scheme by analogy.

limits.parameter_label: Overall pass mark, OHS Practitioner certification examination
limits.display: an overall average mark of at least sixty percent (60%)
limits.qualifier_rule: The overall threshold is necessary but NOT sufficient — it must be achieved together with the per-element minimum below. A candidate averaging 70% but scoring 45% in Element 2 fails.
limits.source_quote: To become a Certified OHS Practitioner, the candidate must obtain an overall average mark of at least sixty percent (60%) provided that the candidate achieved a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark for each of these examination elements - Risk Management (Element 2), Application of Safety Concepts (Element 3), and Health and Safety Regulations (Element 6).
limits.note: Inclusive minimum by the 'at least' glyph. Stated twice, identically, in section 8.4 and again in Annex C.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum per-element mark for the three gated examination elements
limits.display: a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark for each of Element 2 (Risk Management), Element 3 (Application of Safety Concepts) and Element 6 (Health and Safety Regulations)
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to three of the six elements only. Elements 1 (Health and Safety Management System), 4 (Emergency Preparedness and Response) and 5 (Occupational Health and Ergonomics) carry NO individual minimum — a candidate may score zero in any of them and still pass, provided the overall average reaches 60% and the three gated elements each reach 50%.
limits.source_quote: To pass the OHS Practitioner Certification examination, the candidate must obtain an overall average mark of at least sixty percent (60%) provided that the candidate achieved a minimum of fifty percent (50%) mark for each of these examination elements - Risk Management (Element 2), Application of Safety Concepts (Element 3) and Health and Safety Regulations (Element 6).
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. The asymmetry between gated and ungated elements is deliberate in the source and is reproduced exactly rather than smoothed into a uniform rule.

limits.parameter_label: Number of questions in the certification examination
limits.display: 100 multiple choice questions with four (4) possible answers and only one (1) correct answer
limits.qualifier_rule: Element weightings within the 100 questions: Element 1 Health and Safety Management System 15%; Element 2 Risk Management 15%; Element 3 Application of Safety Concepts 20%; Element 4 Emergency Preparedness and Response 10%; Element 5 Occupational Health and Ergonomics 20%; Element 6 Health and Safety Regulations 20%. The weightings total 100%.
limits.source_quote: The OHS Practitioner Certification Scheme Examination contains 100 multiple choice questions with four (4) possible answers and only one (1) correct answer.
limits.note: An exact specification rather than a bound. The six element weightings were checked and do sum to 100 — worth stating because several tables elsewhere in this corpus do not reconcile.

limits.parameter_label: Time allowed for the certification examination
limits.display: should be completed within three (3) hours
limits.qualifier_rule: Closed book — access to any reference material during the examination is not permitted.
limits.source_quote: The examination should be completed within three (3) hours. Access of any reference material during the examination is not permitted.
limits.note: Inclusive upper bound by the 'within' glyph.

limits.parameter_label: Attempts permitted before the whole certification process must be repeated
limits.display: Candidate failing to pass the examination from the first and second attempts can retake the examination by paying only the examination fee each time. However, candidates failing the third time shall repeat the whole process
limits.qualifier_rule: Attempts one and two carry only the examination fee; failing the third means reapplying and being reassessed from the start, per the Annex A flowchart. The document does not state any time limit within which the three attempts must fall.
limits.source_quote: Candidate failing to pass the examination from the first and second attempts can retake the examination by paying only the examination fee (as defined by Dubai Municipality) each time. However, candidates failing the third time shall repeat the whole process (see Annex A)
limits.note: Inclusive at three: the third failure triggers the reset. Note the Annex A flowchart adds a consequence the body text does not spell out — on a third-attempt failure the flowchart branches to 'Company to appoint other employee meeting OHS Practitioner requirement', so a failed third attempt is an EMPLOYER problem, not only a candidate one, and may create a staffing gap the compliance view should surface.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum invigilators per candidates at a certification examination
limits.display: at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to the Certification Body conducting the examination.
limits.source_quote: Certification Body should appoint trained personnel to act as invigilators. Invigilators must arrive at the venue ahead of time and there should be at least one invigilator for every 20 candidates.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Identical figure and near-identical wording to GU131 and to the sibling scheme S2 — a reused DM examination-conduct block.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum separation between candidate desks or computers at a certification examination
limits.display: not less than 1.25 meters apart (measured from the center of the desk/computer)
limits.qualifier_rule: Measured from the centre of the desk or computer. Where candidates share a large desk or the distance cannot be provided, multiple versions of the examination questionnaire SHALL be used — note this document says 'shall' where GU131 says 'should' for the same fallback.
limits.source_quote: Candidates should be seated at separate desks/computers (in case of computer-based examination) that should normally be placed not less than 1.25 meters apart (measured from the center of the desk/computer). In circumstances where candidates share a large desk or when the recommended distance is not possible to be provided, multiple versions of examination questionnaires shall be used.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Extends GU131's wording to computer-based examinations. Hedged by 'should normally' with an explicit stated alternative, so conditional rather than absolute.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum experience — entry route (a), Bachelor's degree in engineering
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies where the candidate holds a Bachelor's degree in engineering together with a government-approved Diploma in Occupational Health and/or Safety, or an international/national Diploma from NEBOSH, BSC, BCSP, Ofqual or NVQ. The shortest of the four routes.
limits.source_quote: Bachelor's degree in engineering; and Diploma in Occupational Health and/or Safety (Government-approved educational qualifications - national or international) with two (2) years of experience; or International or National Diploma NEBOSH / BSC/ BCSP/ Ofqual/ NVQ with two (2) years of experience.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. The document does not say the experience must be in health and safety specifically, nor whether it must be post-qualification — both genuinely open on the text.

limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to route (b) Diploma in Engineering plus an OHS diploma; route (c) Bachelor of Science plus an OHS diploma; and route (d) a government-approved Bachelor's degree in occupational health and safety on a 3 to 4 year curriculum, where the 5 years is expressed as 'work experience'.
limits.source_quote: Diploma in Engineering; and Diploma in Occupational Health and/or Safety ... with five (5) years of experience ... Bachelor of Science; Diploma in Occupational Health and/or Safety ... with five (5) years of experience ... Bachelor's degree in occupational health and safety (Government-approved educational qualifications - national or international) (3 to 4 years curriculum) with five (5) years of work experience.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Note route (d) requires 5 years even though the degree is directly in occupational health and safety, while route (a) requires only 2 years for an engineering degree plus an OHS diploma — the scheme values the engineering degree more highly than the OHS degree, which is counter-intuitive but is what the document says and is reproduced without adjustment.

limits.parameter_label: Required curriculum length of an OHS bachelor's degree under entry route (d)
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies only to entry route (d), the direct occupational health and safety bachelor's degree.
limits.source_quote: Bachelor's degree in occupational health and safety (Government-approved educational qualifications - national or international) (3 to 4 years curriculum) with five (5) years of work experience.
limits.note: Both bounds treated as inclusive on the plain reading of a '3 to 4' range. A degree on a 2-year curriculum does not qualify under this route.

obligations.cadence_note: Two years from date of issuance, with renewal required BEFORE the end of the second year — so the due date is earlier than the expiry date and the app should warn ahead of it. No renewal window length is stated (contrast the Lifeguard scheme's explicit two months) and no grace period is stated either way. The renewal route depends on evidence: submit an employment certificate plus two years of CPD evidence and renewal is documentary; fail to submit and a renewal examination must be taken and passed to the same 60%/50% standard. This is a genuine competency validity, not an examination interval.
obligations.trigger_event: approach of the end of the second year of certification validity; or an unsatisfactory company compliance grade (D or E) at routine DM health and safety inspection where further assessment confirms the practitioner's inability; or a recommendation by the DM OHS Officer conducting inspection monitoring
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS Practitioners at all industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai
obligations.source_quote: OHS Practitioner shall renew the certification before the end of the second year of certification validity. To be considered for certification renewal, the OHS Practitioner shall submit to the Certification Body the following documents that proves continuing competence covering the past two (2) years since the time of certification: Employment certificate as occupational health and safety practitioner; and Activities attended or participated in to improve existing health and safety knowledge ... OHS Practitioners failing to submit the above documentary evidence shall take and pass the certification renewal examination approved by the Health and Safety Department. (p11-12)

obligations.cadence_note: CONTINUING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, ENTIRELY UNQUANTIFIED — no hours, no points, no minimum number of activities and no annual milestone. What is fixed is the assessment period: the evidence must cover the past two years since certification, aligning the CPD record to the certification cycle rather than the calendar year (contrast GU131, whose trainer CPD reports on a fixed 31 December deadline). Recorded as an honest null on cadence. THE PRODUCT ANGLE, worth stating plainly: because sufficient CPD evidence replaces a renewal examination entirely, contemporaneous CPD capture converts a exam sitting into a paperwork submission. That is a direct, demonstrable client benefit and the strongest such case in the corpus.
obligations.trigger_event: renewal of certification (evidence must cover the preceding two years)
obligations.applies_to: Certified OHS Practitioners — activities attended or participated in to improve existing health and safety knowledge: training certificates, training hours, workshops and conferences (private or government), documents proving involvement with professional bodies and campaigns, writing journal articles
obligations.source_quote: Activities attended or participated in to improve existing health and safety knowledge (e.g. certificates of trainings, training hours, workshops and conferences attended (Private / Government), documents proving involvement with professional bodies and campaigns, writing journal articles, etc.). (p11)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing staffing requirement with no interval — every industry in Dubai shall employ Certified OHS Practitioners, and the establishment must ensure the Certification Body's registration of that practitioner with the Department is kept up to date. It becomes due when a post falls vacant, when a certificate expires, or when a third examination failure forces the company to appoint a different employee. A state to be maintained rather than a periodic task. NOTE THE GAP: unlike GU131, which fixes required headcount against room count in a table, this scheme sets NO ratio, NO headcount and NO sizing rule of any kind. It says 'Certified OHS Practitioners' in the plural for every industry regardless of size. So the app can verify that at least one certified practitioner is employed and registered, and cannot judge whether the number employed is adequate. Only DM can close that.
obligations.trigger_event: operation of any industry in Dubai; vacancy in the OHS practitioner post; certificate expiry; third-attempt examination failure
obligations.applies_to: All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai — factories, construction, infrastructure and service sector business entities and establishments
obligations.source_quote: All industries operating in the Emirate of Dubai shall employ Certified OHS Practitioners within their organization to ensure Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) management for the business entity or establishment. All records of registered Certified OHS Practitioner for all types of industries shall be maintained with the Health and Safety Department. The business entity or establishment shall ensure that CB registered OHS Practitioner to the Department is up to date. (p6)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing retain-and-produce duty with no interval and no stated retention period. A SOFT COPY of the OHS Practitioner certification and related health and safety qualifications and training shall be retained in the establishment and provided to official representatives of the Department when required — note the document specifies soft copy, which is unusual and directly supports a document-store implementation. Mapped to 'reporting' as the closest term in the closed vocabulary; the duty is retention and production on demand. Noted per rule 4.
obligations.trigger_event: request by official representatives of the DM Health and Safety Department
obligations.applies_to: Business entities and establishments — soft copy of each OHS Practitioner's certification plus related health and safety qualifications and training records
obligations.source_quote: A soft copy of Certification of OHS Practitioner and related health and safety qualifications and training shall be retained in the establishment and should be provided to the official representatives of the Department when required. (p6)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing access duty, no cadence. Certification Bodies must give the H&S Department access to records and documentation on personnel qualifications and audits, and officials nominated by the Director access to examination question papers, scripts, marking records and associated documents. Separately, the candidate database maintained by the Certification Body must be accessible to Dubai Municipality — note this is framed as standing ACCESS rather than as the periodic submission GU131 requires, a real difference between the two schemes.
obligations.trigger_event: request by the Department or by officials nominated by its Director
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies — records on personnel qualifications and audits, examination papers, scripts and marking records, and the candidate registration database (company name, main activity and sector, location, trade licence number; candidate job designation, age, gender, nationality, language skills, qualifications and experience)
obligations.source_quote: Certification Bodies shall provide the Health and Safety Department with access to records and documentation relating to personnel qualifications and audits. The officials specifically nominated by the Director of the Department shall have access to examination question papers, examination scripts, records of marking and any other relevant documents associated with the certification scheme. (p8-9) A database of candidates shall be maintained by the Certification Bodies and access to this information shall be provided to Dubai Municipality. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven, no cadence. Recorded separately from the competency obligation because the examination has its own conduct and integrity rules and because, on renewal, it applies only to practitioners who fail to produce CPD evidence. 100 multiple choice questions, four options, one correct answer, three hours, closed book, 60% overall with 50% in each of Elements 2, 3 and 6. Three attempts before the whole process must be repeated.
obligations.trigger_event: application for certification; or renewal where documentary evidence of continuing competence is not submitted
obligations.applies_to: OHS Practitioner candidates whose qualifications have been verified and screened by the Certification Body against the section 6 minimum competency requirements
obligations.source_quote: Certification Bodies shall verify and screen candidates' qualifications in accordance with Section 6 of this document. Candidates who fulfill the prescribed minimum competency requirements are allowed to proceed in taking the certification examination (see Annex A). (p9) Certification Bodies shall take appropriate action to ensure that quality and integrity of the examinations and certifications are not compromised. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: No interval stated for either duty. Examination materials must be submitted by the Certification Body to the H&S Department and approved before use (Annex B flowchart); the approval then runs until content is revised, approval is revoked, the body ceases operation or EIAC withdraws its accreditation. The Annex B note says the approval 'is valid for a specified period' AND NEVER SPECIFIES THE PERIOD — an explicit acknowledgement of a validity with the number omitted, which is a documentation defect rather than an extraction gap. Separately, Certification Bodies shall meet ISO 17024 requirements in reviewing the effectiveness of the scheme, again with no stated frequency, and the Department reviews and changes programmes where evaluation shows the scheme's objectives are not achieved.
obligations.trigger_event: content revision of examination materials; revocation of approval; cessation of the Certification Body's operation; withdrawal of EIAC accreditation
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies — DM approval of examination materials in Arabic and English; and review of the effectiveness of the scheme per ISO 17024
obligations.source_quote: Examination materials will be approved by Health and Safety Department unless there is content revision; or approval is revoked earlier by the Department; or the Certification Body ceases its operation; or its accreditation is withdrawn by EIAC. Certification Bodies shall meet the requirements of ISO 17024 standard in reviewing the effectiveness of the scheme. (p8) Note: Issued examination material approval is valid for a specified period unless there is content revision ... (Annex B, p14)

obligations.cadence_note: The scheme refers to 'routine health and safety inspections of Dubai Municipality' and to their company compliance grades, but sets no inspection frequency — that lives in the DM inspection regime, not in this scheme document. Honest null. NOTE THE GRADE SCALE DIFFERS FROM GU131: here the failing grades are D or E, whereas GU131 names D or F for labour accommodations. Two DM documents, two different grade vocabularies; do not normalise them into one scale without checking.
obligations.applies_to: Business entities and establishments — routine DM health and safety inspection. An unsatisfactory company compliance grade (D or E) puts the OHS Practitioner's certificate at risk of cancellation and reassessment where further assessment confirms their inability. The DM OHS Officer conducting inspection monitoring can separately recommend cancellation of the certification.
obligations.source_quote: OHS Practitioners of industries obtaining unsatisfactory company compliance (grade D or E) in the routine health and safety inspections of Dubai Municipality shall be considered for certificate cancellation and reassessment, if further assessment confirms his/her inability. (p12) The DM Occupational Health and Safety Officer designated to conduct inspection monitoring to the business entity or establishment can recommend the cancellation of the OHS Practitioner's certification based on the conditions referred to in this document. (p6-7)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing certificate-content requirement, no cadence. The certificate issued on passing must bear: certification title, name of candidate, date of birth, designation or official job title, TYPE OF SECTOR (construction, factories, service), Emirates ID number, signature of the issuing Certification Body, serial or control number of the certificate, the EIAC symbol, the Dubai Municipality logo and the Certification Body logo. Compare this field list against section 4.4's certificates table: 'type of sector' and 'designation' have no home there, and the sector field in particular is a scoping attribute that may limit where the certificate is valid. The format itself is to be finalised between the Certification Body and the Department, so it is not yet fixed.
obligations.trigger_event: passing the OHS Practitioner certification examination
obligations.applies_to: Certification Bodies issuing OHS Practitioner certificates
obligations.source_quote: On passing the OHS Practitioner Certification Examination, the Certification Body shall issue the certificate bearing the following contents: Certification Title; Name of the candidate; Date of birth; Designation/official job title; Type of sector (Construction, Factories, Service); Emirates ID number; Signature of issuing Certification Body; Serial/control number of the certificate; EIAC symbol; Dubai Municipality logo and Certification Body logo. The Certification Body shall discuss with the Health and Safety Department to finalize the OHS Practitioner certificate format. (p11)
